description.html: The stone skull looks as if it had lain for a long time on a riverbed or in a damp cave. The surface has a yellow-green, moss-like patina, dark cracks across the crown and the rough texture of old stone. Large eye sockets, a nasal opening and a gaping jaw with big teeth give it an expressive, slightly creepy look.

The openings in the skull serve as a hide. In an aquarium, small fish and shrimp swim in and out through them, and the greenish tones blend nicely with plants. In a terrarium, small lizards, geckos and amphibians use it as a shelter, and it works especially well in humid, tropical setups with moss.

Before placing the skull, rinse it with lukewarm water, without soap or chemicals. Set it on a flat bottom and press it lightly into the substrate so it stands steadily. Check that the openings are large enough for your animals so none of them gets stuck. Use a soft brush for cleaning; it removes algae and deposits without damaging the patina. It pairs well with roots, stones and other themed decorations from our equipment range.
